[LeBron James](/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") became an era-defining star during the 2010s, while leading the [Cleveland Cavaliers](/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers") to a historic title in 2016.

After four seasons with the Miami Heat, [LeBron James](/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James") returned to the [Cleveland Cavaliers](/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers") for the 2014–15 season.[[103]](#cite_note-103) He led the team to their second Finals appearance with the help of [Kyrie Irving](/wiki/Kyrie_Irving "Kyrie Irving") and [Kevin Love](/wiki/Kevin_Love "Kevin Love"). The [Golden State Warriors](/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors") defeated the Cavaliers in six games, led by the "[Splash Brothers](/wiki/Splash_Brothers "Splash Brothers")" [Stephen Curry](/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry") and [Klay Thompson](/wiki/Klay_Thompson "Klay Thompson"). The Cavaliers and the Warriors faced each other in the Finals a record [four consecutive times](/wiki/Cavaliers%E2%80%93Warriors_rivalry "Cavaliers–Warriors rivalry").[[104]](#cite_note-104) In the 2015–16 season, the Warriors finished the season 73–9, the [best season record in NBA history](/wiki/List_of_NBA_teams_by_single_season_win_percentage "List of NBA teams by single season win percentage").[[105]](#cite_note-105) However, the Cavaliers overcame a 3–1 deficit in the Finals to win [their first championship](/wiki/2016_NBA_Finals "2016 NBA Finals") that season,[[106]](#cite_note-106) and end a [52-year professional sports championship drought](/wiki/Cleveland_sports_curse "Cleveland sports curse") for the city of [Cleveland](/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland").[[107]](#cite_note-107) In the 2016–17 season, the Warr

fanoutqa_036617.x:
France national football team :: History :: 1950s–1980s :: part 01 :: chunk_0004
France's first '[Golden Generation](/wiki/Golden_Generation "Golden Generation")' in the late 1950s comprised players such as [Just Fontaine](/wiki/Just_Fontaine "Just Fontaine"), [Raymond Kopa](/wiki/Raymond_Kopa "Raymond Kopa"), [Jean Vincent](/wiki/Jean_Vincent_(footballer) "Jean Vincent (footballer)"), [Robert Jonquet](/wiki/Robert_Jonquet "Robert Jonquet"), [Maryan Wisnieski](/wiki/Maryan_Wisnieski "Maryan Wisnieski"), [Thadée Cisowski](/wiki/Thad%C3%A9e_Cisowski "Thadée Cisowski"), and [Armand Penverne](/wiki/Armand_Penverne "Armand Penverne"). At the [1958 World Cup](/wiki/1958_FIFA_World_Cup "1958 FIFA World Cup"), France reached the semi-finals where they lost to [Brazil](/wiki/Brazil_national_football_team "Brazil national football team"). In the 3rd-place match, France defeated West Germany 6–3 with Fontaine recording four goals, which brought his goal tally in the competition to 13, a World Cup record that still stands today. France hosted the inaugural [UEFA European Football Championship](/wiki/UEFA_European_Football_Championship "UEFA European Football Championship") in 1960. For the second straight international tournament, the team reached the semi-finals, but were defeated 5–4 by [Yugoslavia](/wiki/Yugoslavia_national_football_team "Yugoslavia national football team") despite being up 4–2 heading into the 75th minute. In the third-place match, France was defeated 2–0 by Czechoslovakia.

The 1960s and 1970s saw France decline significantly playing under several managers and failing to qualify for numerous international tournaments. On 25 April 1962, [Henri Guérin](/wiki/Henri_Gu%C3%A9rin_(footballer) "Henri Guérin (footballer)") was officially installed as the team's first manager. Kenney went on a local sports talk radio program to respond to Christie's claims. "He's got the biggest 'L' on his forehead of anybody in the country. He ran for president for one hot-mess minute and then when that was over he was moon-dogging Trump thinking he was going to get a big job," Kenney said. In 2004, Messi (pictured in 2005) began his 17-year professional career with [FC Barcelona](/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona")

Messi began the [2004–05 season](/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_FC_Barcelona_season "2004–05 FC Barcelona season") as a guaranteed starter for the [Barcelona B](/wiki/FC_Barcelona_B "FC Barcelona B") team, but after some lobbying by the senior players, he was promoted to the first team by manager [Frank Rijkaard](/wiki/Frank_Rijkaard "Frank Rijkaard").[[57]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013246–249-65) He made his [La Liga](/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") debut for Barcelona on 16 October 2004, at 17 years old.[[42]](#cite_note-Serviette-48) He scored his first senior goal on 1 May 2005, becoming the youngest-ever scorer for the club at the time.[[63]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHunter201235–36-71)[[64]](#cite_note-72) He was at that time the youngest player to represent Barcelona in an official competition, and the club won the [league title](/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_La_Liga "2004–05 La Liga") during that season.[[59]](#cite_note-LastJump-67)[[65]](#cite_note-MessiDriven-73)

On his 18th birthday, Messi signed his first contract as a senior team player, which kept him with Barcelona through 2010, and had a release clause of €150 million.[[66]](#cite_note-:0-74) Three months later, as his performance continued to make waves, his contract was updated to double his salary and keep him with the club until 2014.[[61]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBalagué2013262–263-69)[[67]](#cite_note-Starlet-75) By the end of the [2005–06 season](/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_FC_Barcelona_season "2005–06 FC Barcelona season"), Barcelona had won [La Liga](/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_La_Liga "2005–06 La Liga") again as well as the [UEFA Champions League](/wiki/2005%E2%80%93

West coast of North America

The West Coast of the United States has an [oceanic climate](/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate") in its Northwestern, Northern, and Eastern edge towards the U.S.-Canada border, but from Northern California, towards the U.S.-Mexico border the climate is [Mediterranean](/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate"). While the northern half of the west coast, particularly coastal Washington and Oregon has moderate rainfall, particularly during the winter months, much of coastal California is drier year-round.

The coastline sees significantly milder temperatures compared to inland areas during summer. In far Northern California there is a difference of 17 °C (30 °F) between [Eureka](/wiki/Eureka,_California "Eureka, California") and [Willow Creek](/wiki/Willow_Creek,_California "Willow Creek, California") despite only 25 miles (40 km) separating the locations and Willow Creek being located at a 500 metres (1,600 ft) elevation. Slightly narrower fluctuations can be seen all through the coastline, and could partially be explained by the cold currents in the Pacific Ocean moderating coastal temperatures and the mountain ranges blocking the maritime air from moving farther inland than its foothills during summer.[[12]](#cite_note-blue_planet-13)

[Coastal fog](/wiki/Coastal_fog "Coastal fog") is also prevalent in keeping shoreline temperatures cool.
